name: Character Name Generator
description: Generates unique character names using AI, fixing the commonly reused names issue
instruction: You MUST use the generate_character_name tool whenever a NEW named character enters the story: introducing a new character, a stranger who joins the scene and speaks or acts, anyone who will keep appearing or matters to the plot. Every such character MUST have a name generated by this tool — never make up or invent character names yourself. If multiple new characters appear, call the tool once for each. EXCEPTION — do NOT call this tool for incidental background figures who are only mentioned in passing and need no name (e.g. "a guard", "the shopkeeper", "a girl in the crowd"), or when a name would only be a minor world-building or dialogue detail: leave them unnamed and keep writing the story. Never interrupt or replace the story response just to generate a name.

functions.name: generate_character_name
functions.description: Generate a unique name for a new character. Use this tool when you wish to create a new character and need a name for them.

gender.description: The gender for the character name

culture.description: The cultural origin of the name (e.g. Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Chinese, European, Latin, Norse, African, Indian, etc.)

style.description: The genre/aesthetic style of the name (e.g. fantasy, modern, medieval, sci-fi, mythological, steampunk, etc.)

context.description: Brief context about the character or story to help generate a fitting name

name.description: A single generated character name in the chat's language script

technical.execution: Runs a small nested AI call with randomized constraints (starting letter, syllable count) and a blocklist of overused names, so names stay unique. Adds a small AI cost and about a second of latency per call.
technical.persistence: Each call and its result are stored on the message and replayed to the AI in later turns.

name: Dice Roll
description: Rolls real dice (d4 to d20) for uncertain actions, so outcomes are decided by true randomness instead of the AI choosing
instruction: When the current action has an uncertain outcome, call roll_dice BEFORE narrating the result, then narrate honestly from the numbers: high rolls succeed, low rolls fail, the die's maximum is a critical success, 1 is a critical failure. Use a d20 for action checks by default; use smaller dice (d4 to d12) when a mechanic calls for them, e.g. amounts, degrees or random tables. For pass/fail checks, decide the target number BEFORE rolling and pass it as dc together with the character's flat bonus as modifier, plus modifierBreakdown naming its parts (e.g. "Agility +3, well equipped +1"): the server computes success and the roll card shows it to the player. Set characterName when the roll is a specific character's attempt; omit it for scenario rolls (weather, encounters, luck). Supporting rolls (amounts, bulk secondary rolls, table lookups) should be minor: true so the player only sees the rolls that decide outcomes; d20 action checks stay featured. Never re-roll, ignore, or make up dice values.

functions.name: roll_dice
functions.description: Roll one or more real dice. Use whenever an action's outcome is uncertain and should be decided by chance (attempts, contests, luck). The d20 is the default check die; pick a smaller die when the story mechanic calls for it (amounts, random tables, splitting outcomes). Never invent or alter dice results.

rolls.description: The dice rolls to make, one entry per uncertain action

reason.description: Short description of what this roll decides, e.g. "Kade tries to pick the lock"

die.description: Which die to roll. Default d20.

characterName.description: The character this roll belongs to, when it is a specific character's attempt. Omit for scenario rolls (weather, random events, luck of the situation).

advantage.description: Roll twice and take the higher (advantage) or lower (disadvantage) result. Default none.

dc.description: Target number to meet or beat (the difficulty or threshold of the attempt). When set, the server judges the roll (success = die value + modifier >= dc; the die's maximum always succeeds, a natural 1 always fails) and the roll card displays success or fail.

modifier.description: Flat bonus added to the die value before comparing against dc (the character's relevant bonus for this attempt). Default 0.

modifierBreakdown.description: What the modifier is made of, e.g. "Agility +3, well equipped +1". ALWAYS include it when modifier is non-zero; shown to the player with the roll.

minor.description: Supporting roll shown only in a collapsed list, not as its own card. Default: false for d20, true for smaller dice. Set true for bookkeeping d20 batches (e.g. a whole group rolling at once); set false for a smaller-die roll that alone decides an outcome.

die.description: The die that was rolled (d4 to d20)

character.description: Echoed characterName when the roll is character-specific

value.description: Final result, 1 up to the die's maximum (max = critical success, 1 = critical failure)

dice.description: Raw die values; two entries when rolled with advantage or disadvantage

minor.description: Supporting roll: shown collapsed in chat instead of as its own card (default true for non-d20 dice)

dc.description: Echoed target number when the request set one

modifierBreakdown.description: Echoed composition of the modifier, shown on the roll card

total.description: value + modifier; present when dc or modifier was set

success.description: Server verdict vs dc: total >= dc, with the die's maximum always true and a natural 1 always false. Shown on the roll card.

technical.execution: Runs instantly on the server using cryptographically secure randomness. No extra AI call, no added cost. Max 50 rolls per call; advantage/disadvantage rolls two dice and keeps the higher/lower.
technical.persistence: Each call and its results are stored on the message and replayed to the AI in later turns, so past rolls stay consistent.

name: Character Stats
description: Keeps persistent character sheets: the AI reads and updates each character's stats, inventory and skills as the story progresses
instruction: Keep character sheets in sync with the story: read_character_stats before referencing a character's stats, items or skills; update_character_stats immediately when the story changes a sheet (a value moves, something is gained or lost, an ability is learned or forgotten). How stats work: effective stat = base "value" + numeric offset. For depleting stats (HP, MP, meters) the value IS the maximum — never change it for temporary loss or recovery. Report each change as a "delta", the amount from THIS event only ("-7" after 7 damage, "5" after healing 5); the server accumulates it (value 20 after delta "-5" reads 15/20, a later delta "-7" reads 8/20). "modifier" instead SETS the absolute total offset ("0" = fully restored) — never send one event's amount as modifier. Change the value only when the true maximum permanently changes; plain counters (currency, ranks) just set the value. Keep changes proportionate to the event and never narrate numbers that contradict the sheet. The free-text Custom section is the creator's catch-all (notes, trackers, relationships — possibly markdown): maintain it in the spirit the existing text establishes, updating via "custom" with the FULL rewritten section. Route data: tracked values in stats, possessions in inventory, learnable abilities in skills, everything else in Custom. upsertStats and upsertSkills CREATE OR UPDATE by name. removeStats deletes ad-hoc tracker stats only (schema stats cannot be removed). "reset": true wipes a botched sheet to rebuild it in the same entry — never for normal story changes. Every character in the action needs an initialized sheet: the moment one becomes relevant, initialize their full stats (a value for every tracked stat) in one call before applying changes. Only update when something ACTUALLY changed: never re-send a current value, a zero delta or an identical modifier.

functions.name: read_character_stats
functions.description: Read the current character sheet (stats, inventory and skills) of one or more specific characters by name. Call this before referencing a character's numbers, possessions or abilities so the story stays consistent with the tracked data.

characterNames.description: Names of the characters whose sheets to read. List every character the scene needs in ONE call.

functions.name: update_character_stats
functions.description: Update character sheets when the story changes them: stat values (damage, healing, level ups), inventory (items gained, lost, bought, sold, equipped), skills (learned or forgotten) and the free-text Custom section. Apply changes right after the event happens in the story.

changes.description: One entry per character being updated

characterName.description: The character whose sheet changes. Must match an existing character's name.

reason.description: Short in-story reason for this change, e.g. "Took 5 slashing damage from the bandit" or "Bought a healing potion". Shown to the player.

reset.description: Wipe this character's ENTIRE sheet (all stats, inventory, skills and Custom) before applying the rest of this entry. Use ONLY to rebuild a sheet that was set up wrong; provide the corrected full sheet in the same entry.

upsertStats.description: Stats to create or update (upsert by name), e.g. HP, Gold, Level, Status. Provide "value", "delta" and/or "modifier"; the effective stat = value + modifier.

value.description: The base value (overwrites). For capped stats like HP this is the MAXIMUM; set it on creation or real growth (level ups), NOT for damage or healing. Write numbers as plain digits, e.g. "20".

delta.description: NUMBER stats only. Relative change to the current value: the amount from THIS event only, e.g. "-7" after taking 7 damage, "5" after healing 5. The server adds it onto the stat's accumulated offset — no math needed. PREFERRED for damage, healing and any incremental change. For text/enum/boolean stats set "value" instead.

modifier.description: ABSOLUTE total offset from the base value (current = value + modifier); overwrites the previous offset, it does NOT add. Use "0" to mark a depleted stat fully restored. For incremental damage or healing use "delta" instead.

removeStats.description: Names of stats to remove from the sheet entirely, for temporary trackers that stop existing (a ritual progress bar, a disguise meter). Stats declared in the storyline's stat schema cannot be removed, set their value instead.

addItems.description: Items gained. Adding an item the character already has increases its quantity.

equipped.description: Whether the character equips it now

removeItems.description: Items lost, used or sold. Removing fewer than the held quantity decreases it; otherwise the item is removed.

quantity.description: How many removed. Omit to remove the item entirely.

upsertSkills.description: Skills or abilities to create or update (upsert by name): new ones learned, or an existing one whose description changed (rank up, new effect).

removeSkills.description: Names of skills forgotten or lost

custom.description: FULL replacement of the character's free-text Custom section (notes, trackers, markdown; the creator defines its purpose). Rewrite the whole section keeping still-relevant content; empty string clears it. Max 4000 characters.

characters.description: The requested character sheets keyed by character name

stats.description: Tracked stats: { name, type, base, modifier? }

inventory.description: Held items: { name, quantity, description, equipped }

unknownCharacters.description: Requested names that matched no character in the chat

characters.description: The updated character sheets keyed by character name (same shape as read_character_stats)

changes.description: Per-character before/after summary of what was applied ({ character, reset, stats: [{ name, from, to }], statsRemoved, itemsAdded, itemsRemoved, skillsAdded, skillsRemoved, customUpdated }). The chat shows it as a "stats updated" card on the message.

issues.description: Rejected or skipped changes with the reason (unknown stat, type mismatch, no-op)

unknownCharacters.description: Requested names that matched no character in the chat (their changes were skipped)

technical.execution: Runs instantly on the server. No extra AI call, no added cost. Max 50 characters per read call, 10 per update call. Shares its data with the Dungeon Mind: both read and write the same per-chat character sheets.
technical.persistence: Sheets are saved on the message where they change, so retries and branch switches roll the data back together with the story. Characters whose authored profile includes sheets start from those sheets. The in-chat character sheet UI displays the tracked data.

name: Character Manager
description: Creates new story characters with AI-generated portraits and keeps them up to date as the story evolves: name reveals and description changes
instruction: Call create_character for EVERY new INDIVIDUAL that appears in the story with any presence, human or not: people, monsters, beasts, spirits, constructs, anything that acts or is interacted with. Named or unnamed (use a descriptor with location for unnamed ones, e.g. "guard (north gate)" or "owlbear (dark forest)"). One call per individual, never for characters that already exist. Mark throwaway individuals (mob monsters, random enemies, one-scene NPCs) with extra: true. Call edit_character when an existing character's name changes in the story (their real name is revealed, an alias is dropped, or they are renamed) or when the story permanently changes a character: update their character note with lasting developments (injuries, changed loyalties, new titles, important relationships). The note replaces the previous one, so carry forward still-relevant older points. Only edit on real story developments, never cosmetically.

functions.name: create_character
functions.description: ALWAYS call this tool whenever ANY new INDIVIDUAL character appears in your story — whether named or unnamed. This includes NPCs, monsters, creatures, beasts, or any entity with direct involvement in the story (combat, dialogue, interaction). Creates ONE character with an anime-style image. Call once per character. NEVER create a group — each character must be created separately with their own name and appearance (e.g. "Bandit Leader", "Bandit (east flank)", "Bandit (west flank)").

name.description: Character name. Named characters: proper name (e.g. "Sarah", "Captain Blake"). Unnamed characters: descriptor with location (e.g. "guard (north gate)", "merchant (marketplace, fruit seller)").

isNamed.description: true if the character has a proper name, false if only a descriptor.

extra.description: true for an EXTRA — a throwaway character with no lasting story importance: mob monsters, random quest enemies, one-scene NPCs. Omit or false for characters with ongoing presence in the story. When unsure, use true for anything likely to be gone within a scene or two.

gender.description: Character gender. For non-humanoid entities, pick the gender that best matches their voice/persona.

ageGroup.description: Character age group. For non-humanoid entities, pick the age group that best matches their voice/persona (e.g. ancient dragon = senior, young wolf pup = young).

description.description:
Structured character card (up to 500 words). Adapt fields to the character type:

**Humanoid** (human, elf, demon, etc.):
Name, Age, Race, Gender, Occupation, Background, Personality, Height, Build, Face Shape, Eye Size/Shape/Color, Hair Color/Length/Style, Skin Tone, Outfit, Accessories, Notable Features

**Non-humanoid** (monster, beast, creature, spirit, object, vehicle, plant, etc.):
Name, Type/Species, Size, Shape/Form, Surface (scales, fur, metal, wood, etc.), Key Features (limbs, wings, wheels, leaves, etc.), Face/Front (eyes, mouth, markings, or lack thereof), Distinguishing Details, Demeanor/Behavior

If the story doesn't describe much, MAKE UP appealing details. Be very specific about every visual feature.

imageDescription.description: Detailed visual description starting with name — format: "[Name], [what it is], [appearance details]" (e.g. "Elara, female knight in silver plate armor with blue cape" or "Shadowfang, massive black wolf with glowing red eyes" or "Truck-kun, sentient red semi-truck with glowing headlight eyes and a cracked chrome grill")

imagePrompt.description:
Detailed image generation prompt. START WITH name and what it is.

**Humanoid**: name, gender, height/build, face shape, eye details, skin tone, hair, full outfit with colors/materials, accessories. END WITH: ", full body head to toe shot, poker face, modern anime style, plain solid contrasting background".

**Non-humanoid**: name, type/species, size, shape/form, surface (scales, fur, metal, wood, etc.), key features (limbs, wings, wheels, leaves, etc.), face/front details, distinguishing marks. END WITH: ", full body shot, modern anime style, plain solid contrasting background".

No props, no furniture, no environment. Isolated subject only.

SFW ONLY: the character is always fully clothed or covered in the portrait, in an outfit that fits their role and world. No nudity, no underwear or lingerie, no sexual pose, whatever the story or the player says.

functions.name: edit_character
functions.description: Edit an existing character in this chat: rename them (a name is revealed, an alias is dropped) and/or replace their character note, a custom note for keeping permanent information about them. Works on any character in the chat; the original character card is never modified.

characterName.description: Current name of the character, exactly as it was created

newName.description: The new name (omit to keep the current name)

characterNote.description: A custom note for keeping permanent information about this character. Replaces the previous note, so include still-relevant older points. Max 2000 characters.

extra.description: Reclassify a story character: true marks them an extra (throwaway NPC/mob), false promotes them to a regular character (use when an extra gains lasting story importance).

functions.name: disable_character
functions.description: Remove a character from active play when they PERMANENTLY leave the story: died for good, departed forever, written out. Their card and history are kept but they stop appearing in the story context. Never use it for temporary absences (off-screen, captured, traveling). Player characters can never be disabled.

characterName.description: Current name of the character to disable, exactly as known in the chat

reason.description: Short in-story reason, e.g. "Fell in the siege of Karth". Shown to the player.

image.description: URL of the generated portrait (shown on the chat card)

updated.description: Which parts changed ({ name: { from, to }, characterNote: true, extra: true|false })

knownCharacters.description: On an unknown name: every character in the chat that CAN be edited

disabled.description: True when the character was removed from active play

knownCharacters.description: On an unknown name: every active character that CAN be disabled

error.description: What went wrong (player characters can never be disabled)

technical.execution: create_character generates a full-body anime portrait with the selected image model and waits for it (several seconds); image generation is billed like scene images. The creator and the player can each pick the image model, or "No image" to create characters without portraits at no image cost. edit_character name and description changes are instant.
technical.persistence: Created characters live on the chat itself: they join the cast list for the whole chat, can talk and act like any character, and survive branch switches. Renames work on ANY character, never modify anything else, and keep the previous names so the story stays consistent. Players can edit each character's chat-local character note in the edit-character page; the AI reads it alongside the card.

name: Codex
description: The story's knowledge base: the AI reads creator-written lore and details exactly when the story needs them, and keeps creator-designed records (quest logs, trackers) up to date
instruction: The codex is the story's knowledge base. The index lists each entry with a one-line description: that description tells you what the entry covers and when to read it. Whenever the story is about to touch what a description mentions (a place, faction, rule, past event), call read_codex with the relevant slugs BEFORE writing, and never contradict or invent details a codex entry defines. Keep writable entries up to date with update_codex as the story progresses (quest progress, tracked events, evolving records); preserve the entry's format and still-relevant older information. For small changes to a long entry send targeted "edits" (each oldText copied verbatim from the entry) instead of rewriting the whole content; use "content" only when most of the entry changes. Update only on real story developments.

functions.name: read_codex
functions.description: Read the full content of codex entries by slug (from the codex index).

slugs.description: Slugs of the entries to read (from the codex index)

functions.name: update_codex
functions.description: Update a writable codex entry (marked [writable] in the index): send targeted "edits" (preferred, especially for long entries) or "content" to replace the whole entry. The entry must have been read with read_codex earlier in the same turn.

slug.description: Slug of the writable entry to update

edits.description: Targeted changes, applied in order to the current content. Much cheaper than resending the whole entry: use this for small changes to long entries. Send "edits" OR "content", not both.

oldText.description: The exact text to replace, copied VERBATIM from the entry (including whitespace and line breaks). Must appear exactly once in the entry: include enough surrounding text to make it unique.

newText.description: The replacement text. An empty string deletes oldText.

content.description: The complete new content for the entry (replaces the whole entry). For small changes to a long entry use "edits" instead.

functions.name: create_codex
functions.description: Create a new codex entry with a title, a one-line index description, and full content. The entry becomes readable and updatable by slug.

title.description: Short entry title, e.g. "The Oath at Blackwater"

description.description: ONE line saying what the entry covers and when to read it (this is all you will see in the index later)

category.description: Where the entry sorts in the codex browser. Default lore.

functions.name: delete_codex
functions.description: Delete a codex entry YOU created earlier (a duplicate, or one made obsolete). Creator-authored entries cannot be deleted.

slug.description: Slug of the AI-created entry to delete

entries.description: The requested entries as { slug, title, content, tokens, readOut? } with LIVE content (including AI updates). Every read renders a card in chat with its token count (readOut entries start expanded, others collapsed); hidden entries render only a locked card with title and token count, never their content.

joinedCharacters.description: Characters attached to the read entries that just JOINED the chat ({ name, description }): added to the cast with their full authored profile, like the settings character import. Introduce them naturally.

note.description: Skipped slugs (unknown, or read-once entries already read)

updated.description: Slug of the updated entry (drives the updated-entry chat card)

editsApplied.description: How many targeted edits were applied (edits-mode calls only)

readOut.description: Present when the entry is read-out: the updated-content card starts expanded

error.description: What went wrong (e.g. updating a non-writable entry, updating before reading, or an oldText that did not match — with guidance to correct the call)

created.description: Server-generated slug of the new entry (used to read/update it later)

error.description: What went wrong (e.g. the codex is full)

deleted.description: Slug of the deleted AI-created entry

error.description: What went wrong (creator entries cannot be deleted)

technical.execution: Runs instantly on the server. No extra AI call, no added cost. Max 25 entries per read call.
technical.persistence: Creator entries are authored on the storyline and never modified by play. AI updates to writable entries are stored per chat as an overlay; reads always return the live content. Read-only entries ride the prompt as a one-line index (they cost nothing until the AI actually reads them); writable entries ride with their full content, refreshed at each chapter, so the AI keeps records up to date without extra read calls.

name: Story Ending
description: Lets the AI close the story with a proper ending: the chat ends with an ending card and no further turns, unless the player reverts or restarts
instruction: When the story has truly concluded, narrate the final scene completely, then call end_story once as the very last action of that response, with a fitting title and endingType. Do not call it early: a setback, a chapter ending, a time skip or a cliffhanger is not an ending. Once end_story is called nothing more can be written in this chat, so make sure every thread the ending needs is resolved in the narration before the call.

functions.name: end_story
functions.description: End the story. Call ONLY when the story has reached its definitive conclusion (the goal is achieved or lost for good, the protagonist's journey is over, or the creator's ending conditions are met) and ONLY after the final scene has been fully narrated in this same response. This is the last thing that happens in the chat: the player cannot continue after it. Never use it for chapter breaks, time skips, cliffhangers or pauses.

title.description: Short title of this ending, shown on the ending card, e.g. "The Crown Returns" or "Alone at the Lighthouse"

endingType.description: Tone of the ending: happy, bittersweet, tragic, neutral, true (the canonical ending), or secret (a hidden ending the player unlocked).

epilogue.description: One to three closing sentences for the ending card: where the characters end up after the final scene. Optional; keep the full ending narration in the message itself.

ended.description: Always true: the chat is now ended

technical.execution: Runs instantly on the server; no extra AI call, no added cost. The response stops right after the call, so the AI must finish the ending narration before calling it.
technical.persistence: The ending lives on the message that called it. The chat refuses new turns while that message is the latest one; erasing or retrying it, branching from an earlier message or restarting the chat lifts the ending.

name: Scene Illustrator
description: Lets the story AI commission an illustration of a moment it chooses, drawn from its own visual brief with the characters' reference portraits
instruction: Use illustrate_scene at most once per response and only at moments worth a full-page illustration: a dramatic reveal, a climactic clash, an emotional beat, a striking location, a character's memorable entrance. Most responses need no illustration. You are the art director: the brief you write IS the picture, so describe one frozen instant in concrete visual terms (camera, placement, poses, expressions, environment, lighting, mood) and name the characters exactly as the story spells their names. Never announce the illustration, describe it, or refer to it in your narration; it appears on its own.

functions.name: illustrate_scene
functions.description: Commission ONE illustration of the moment you are narrating right now. You are the art director: write the complete visual brief yourself. The image is drawn with the named characters' reference portraits and appears under this message on its own. Call it at most once per response and only at key moments. Never mention the illustration, describe it, or refer to it in your narration.

description.description: The complete visual brief, 4 to 8 sentences, of ONE frozen instant (never a sequence of events): the camera angle and shot size; where each character stands in the frame and relative to the others; each character's pose, hands, facial expression and eye direction; clothing or physical state only where it differs from usual; the environment (architecture or nature, ground, sky, weather, time of day); the light sources, their direction and the mood. No dialogue and no written text of any kind. Refer to characters by their exact names. SFW ONLY: never brief nudity or a sex act. For an intimate moment, brief the characters clothed or covered (a robe, a sheet, shoulders up), the moment before or after, or a cutaway such as a closed door or a candle burning down.

characters.description: Exact names of the characters visible in the frame, most important first, spelled as the story spells them. Only characters that exist in the story. An empty list draws the environment alone.

perspective.description: "pov" = seen through the player character's eyes (the player is not drawn, others may face the viewer). "third-person" = cinematic outside camera, the player is drawn like everyone else. Omit to use the chat's illustration perspective.

continuePrevious.description: true when this moment keeps the previous illustration's location and cast with small changes (someone enters or leaves, the light shifts, a new action): the previous image is edited instead of redrawn. Omit or false for a new scene.

status.description: "queued": the illustration is drawn after the response completes

characters.description: Named characters that have a portrait and will be drawn

unknownCharacters.description: Named characters with no portrait in this story; they are left out of the picture

technical.execution: Records the brief instantly; no image is rendered inside the response. Once the response completes, the app renders the illustration through the light-novel pipeline (character look tracking, reference portraits, the chat's light-novel image model and perspective) and bills it like a light-novel illustration: the image model's cost plus a small prompt step.
technical.persistence: The brief lives on the message that called it and the illustration attaches under that message and in the chat gallery. Retrying, editing or branching the message discards it like any other message media.

name: Dungeon Mind (DM)
description: Dungeon Mind (DM) that resolves actions using d20 RPG rules with dice rolls and stat tracking

functions.name: engage_dungeon_mind
functions.description: Engage the Dungeon Mind (DM) to resolve any situation that requires dice rolls, stat changes, or rule adjudication. The DM handles all game mechanics. Takes NO arguments — call with an empty object {}.
